CROSS-CHECKS ON THE TWO BIG MOVES (both confirmed, Reuters-originated):
- GOLD DOWN. Reuters, 28 Sep 03:57 GMT: "Gold prices fell more than 2% on Monday as a rise in oil
  prices heightened inflation concerns and reinforced expectations of further Federal Reserve
  interest-rate hikes. Spot gold was down 2.1% at $4,198.10 per ounce... on track for its biggest
  daily decline since September 1." Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade: "The high bond
  yields and high oil price tandem continues to act as a thorn in gold's side."
  Investing.com (approved, data only), 00:42 GMT: XAU/USD -1.1% to $4,236.33; silver -1.7% to
  $63.24; Dollar Index 100.97. Gold has kept falling into the European morning, so CNBC's
  4,176.56 / -2.56% at 07:36 BST is the latest and is consistent with the direction and magnitude.
- OIL UP. Reuters (Florence Tan), 28 Sep 22:02 GMT dateline Singapore: "Brent crude futures rose
  $1.82, or 1.74%, to $106.14 a barrel by 2202 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at
  $93.55 a barrel, up $1.14, or 1.23%." Investing.com, 01:09 GMT: Brent Nov -1.1%... (sic, +1.1%)
  to $105.48. Oil continued rising through the Asian session to 107.04.

CONTEXT FOR THE DRIVERS (Reuters-originated, carried by Investing.com which is approved for data):
- The Fed raised rates in mid-September by 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%. Traders price roughly 65-70% odds
  of another hike in October (CME FedWatch).
- US 10-year real yield 2.83% on 25 September. The 10y-2y spread narrowed to as little as 17bp last
  week, the smallest since early 2025.
- Dollar Index above 101, a two-to-three-month high.
- Kpler preliminary data: Middle East crude exports rebounded to 12.8m bpd in September, the highest
  since the war began in February, with Hormuz flows set to reach about 7.4m bpd as Saudi Arabia
  diverted exports from Yanbu to Ras Tanura after attacks damaged its East-West pipeline.
- US data this week: job openings, ADP, PCE and nonfarm payrolls.

*** WEDNESDAY WARNING — BRENT CONTRACT ROLL ***
ICE Brent Nov'26 (@LCO.1) EXPIRES 30 SEPTEMBER. Dec'26 (@LCO.2) is at 98.91, i.e. $8.13 BELOW the
front month. When the front month rolls, the ticker will appear to fall about $8 overnight. That is
a contract change, NOT a price fall. Do not write it up as one.

FX NOTE: open.er-api.com (snapshot 28 Sep 00:02 UTC) gives GBPUSD 1.323463, which matches CNBC's
1.3234 exactly, and EURGBP 0.860225 against CNBC's 0.8595. The two providers have disagreed on
euro-sterling by roughly 0.0007 all weekend while agreeing exactly on cable. CNBC's reading is the
later and live one, so it is used. Yesterday evening's edition published 0.8604 on the strength of
the ECB daily reference rate and er-api; no Monday ECB fixing exists yet.
Yahoo's chart API returned no parseable JSON on every symbol, second day running.
